//hooks: SHARED floor hooks. SessionStart (matcher 'startup' ONLY) runs TWO commands that — like all Claude Code hooks — execute IN PARALLEL with no ordering guarantee: (1) session.py start — the mechanical session-start ritual (git-state diagnosis, machine detect, time, next-session number, evidence-based orphan triage, write the start stamp) per ADR-0020/ADR-0035, injecting CANON.md + STANDARD.md + the prior handoff entry + user profile as additionalContext per ADR-0022/ADR-0024/ADR-0035, and STAGING the user-visible banner into a per-session file keyed by the stdin session_id; (2) session.py announce — POLLS for that per-session file (bounded, fail-open) and prints the banner (start stamp + any just-auto-closed orphan's end stamp) to plain stdout, the one SessionStart channel that renders to the user, since hookSpecificOutput.systemMessage is upstream-broken (#9090/#50542). announce must POLL, not assume start already ran: they race. Keying the file by session_id makes a stale prior-session banner impossible (the v2.21.0 shared-announce.txt bug, session 59). Split into two hooks so start's own stdout stays pure JSON. A THIRD startup hook, standard_check.py --status (ADR-0047), runs the member's LOCAL standard-version self-check (read-only, fail-open) and prints a one-line signal to stdout — the ring-1 self-check the federation's fleet reconciliation (curate/standard_version.py) mirrors fleet-wide. A FOURTH startup hook, session.py apply-briefs (ADR-0039 Fork A, floor-promoted session 66), auto-adopts conforming Apply:auto briefs from the member's inbox (CFG['inbox']) before the model wakes and surfaces the rest — deterministic, whole-brief-atomic, never-commit (the session-end close commits, so a bad apply shows in git diff), fail-open, and a no-op when a member declares no inbox. The inbox is machine-local (proposed-edits/ is gitignored, delivered over the shared volume per ADR-0027), so it does not race the start hook's git pull. This is the fleet-wide half of zero-touch adoption: every member with the shipped session.py auto-adopts, not just the federation. Both session.py hooks WRITE/read handoff state, so must not fire on resume/clear — hence the 'startup' matcher. The Stop, PreToolUse-heartbeat, and SessionEnd hooks maintain the ADR-0036 liveness sidecar (.session-state/, gitignored): Stop runs session.py heartbeat after every assistant turn, and an unmatchered (all-tools) PreToolUse entry runs the SAME command on every tool call (ADR-0054 — Stop fires only BETWEEN turns, so one long working turn made a live session look crashed and get falsely reaped; tool calls beat constantly DURING a turn; writes are throttled in-command to one per minute). SessionEnd runs session.py record-end to mark a clean exit (fires on clean termination but NOT on crash — the discriminator the next start's auto-triage uses). The FIRST heartbeat of a session also MATERIALIZES its lazy start (ADR-0055): the hook-path `start` defers all mutating work (journal write, handoff compile, reap, auto-push) behind a .pending-start marker, and the first beat — a signal a phantom SessionStart (the desktop-app pre-spawn class) never produces — completes it; phantoms are thereby no-ops by construction. All are fast + fail-open. Systems that run extra SessionStart probes (e.g. the federation's curate/reconcile status hooks) or their own PreToolUse guards add them via settings_extras.hooks (keyed by event), never here.
//pretooluse: Two PreToolUse STRUCTURAL GUARDS plus one unmatchered LIVENESS HEARTBEAT (session.py heartbeat on every tool call — not a guard, never denies; see //hooks and ADR-0054), all reading the hook JSON on stdin and FAILING OPEN on any error. (1) Bash -> session.py check-bash: DENIES (a) any top-level &&/||/;/newline compound (the no-compound-bash universal habit, parent P7; any 2+-operation chain, not just git — a git mutating op in the chain gets a more specific message), and (b) any DESTRUCTIVE single git op (force/mirror/delete push, reset --hard/--keep, force branch delete, interactive/onto rebase, filter-branch/-repo, clean -f, update-ref -d, reflog expire, gc --prune) classified AFTER stripping `git -C <path>`/wrappers, so it catches the `git -C <repo> …` forms the prefix-anchored deny-list below cannot match (confirm-destructive-ops / P9). Parser is quote/heredoc/command-substitution aware (a commit message containing ;/&& is allowed). (1c) AFTER (1a)/(1b) clear, check-bash AUTO-APPROVES the safe git surface (permissionDecision 'allow') — the read-only + forward-only verbs that mirror the floor's plain-git allow-list — so `git -C <path> <verb>` stops prompting (no allow-string can match it; see //git-c). Parity, not new trust: destructive git is denied at (1b) FIRST, and a hook 'allow' can't override a settings deny. (2) AskUserQuestion -> session.py check-question: the guard for the recommend-then-confirm preference (users/<id>/profile.md) — DENIES the multiple-choice picker so questions are asked in prose, not chip UI. It does NOT affect harness permission prompts (a separate mechanism). Both enforce by substrate instead of self-discipline (P15 / add-structural-guard-on-recurrence).

The operative suppression is therefore NOT a settings string but the check-bash PreToolUse hook (see //pretooluse (1c)), which AUTO-APPROVES the safe git surface (permissionDecision 'allow'). The `Bash(git -C:*)` / `Bash(git -C *)` entries below are retained as a harmless documented fallback (they'd start working if CC ever fixes the matcher) but are inert today.
